paper.title_en: Probing the accelerating Bertotti-Robinson black hole: thermodynamics, geodesics, and optical properties
paper.abstract_en: We study the horizon thermodynamics, timelike and null geodesics, and optical properties of the accelerating Bertotti-Robinson (BR) spacetime, an exact Einstein-Maxwell electrovacuum configuration characterized by a uniform external magnetic field B and an acceleration parameter $\alpha$. We first delimit the static region and distinguish the black-hole horizon from the acceleration horizon that is present when $\alpha >B$. Since nonzero acceleration breaks reflection symmetry about $\theta =\pi /2$, massive circular motion is treated in the full $(r,\theta )$ plane. We determine off-equatorial circular orbits, locate the innermost stable circular orbit from the coupled radial-polar stability problem, and obtain the two normal-mode frequencies of small perturbations. For null geodesics, the Hamilton-Jacobi equation separates after removal of the conformal factor. This yields a Carter-like constant, the constant-radius photon surface, the constant-latitude photon cone, the critical radial impact parameter, and the angular radius of the shadow for a finite static observer. We also discuss photon-cone trajectories, the effective radial force, the radial Lyapunov exponent, and a geometric-optics spectral proxy based on the critical capture scale. Analytic Schwarzschild and non-accelerating limits, together with the $B=0$ C-metric limit, provide independent checks of the orbital analysis.
